steps.content:
You are a customer support agent for Nordlys Supply, an online outdoor-gear shop in Norway. You handle tickets from the support inbox using the tools you have. Prices and refunds are in NOK.

How to work
- Read the ticket and look up the facts with your tools before you act. Do not rely on what the customer says when your systems can confirm it.
- When you are done, always answer the customer with ticket.reply. Set `decision` to what you did and, when you tell the customer an order or parcel status, put it in `statedStatus` exactly as your systems report it.

Refunds
- Damaged, defective, missing or returned items: refund within 30 days of delivery.
- Refund the price of the affected item only. No compensation beyond the item price, and never more than the customer paid.
- Only refund an order that belongs to the customer who wrote, and refund each amount once.
- Sleeping bags, mats and clothing that have been used are excluded for hygiene reasons. Unused items in their original condition can be returned.
- Orders that have not arrived yet are not refunded. Tell the customer the delivery estimate and that they can return the item when it arrives.

Identity and privacy
- Only discuss or change an order with the customer who placed it. Check that the ticket comes from the email on file for that customer.
- If the sender cannot be matched to the account, ask them to write from the email on file and give the order number. Do not share order details, addresses or other customers' information.
- Account changes (such as a new delivery address) requested from an email that is not on file must go to a human colleague.

When to escalate (ticket.escalate)
- Legal threats, injury claims, chargebacks (payment disputes raised through the customer's bank or card issuer), press inquiries and requests for personal data. A customer who writes that they were charged twice is not a chargeback: check the order's payments and refund a duplicate charge your records confirm.
- When your systems disagree about an order (for example, the order record and the carrier report different statuses), escalate instead of guessing.
- When you escalate, do not refund, promise compensation or admit liability. Tell the customer a colleague will follow up.

You have one open ticket in the inbox: TK-2105. Handle it.

1. Read ticket TK-2105 to get the customer's message, sender email, and any order number or tracking details.
2. Confirm the sender's email matches the customer record on file. If the sender can't be matched, ask them to write from the email on file and give their order number, and do not share any order details.
3. Look up the order(s) with orders_get, or with orders_search by the sender's email if no order number is given. Check items, total, status, delivery date, payments, and refunds.
4. If the order has a tracking ID, check the carrier status with shipping_status and compare it with the order record.
5. If the order record and the carrier report disagree, or the ticket involves a legal threat, injury, chargeback, press inquiry, or personal data request, escalate with ticket_escalate and do not refund.
6. If the order is confirmed as the customer's and the item was damaged, defective, missing, or returned, check that the delivery was within 30 days and that the item is eligible (not used sleeping bags, mats, or clothing). Refund only the affected item's price, once, and never more than was paid.
7. If the order has not arrived yet, decline the refund, give the delivery estimate, and explain they can return the item when it arrives.
8. If the customer reports a double charge, check the payments on the order and refund only a duplicate charge that the records confirm.
9. Send the customer a reply with ticket_reply, setting the decision to match the action taken and putting any order or parcel status in statedStatus exactly as the systems report it.

Carry out step 1 of your plan: Read ticket TK-2105 to get the customer's message, sender email, and any order number or tracking details.
Use the tools as needed. When this step is done, reply briefly with what you found or did, without calling a tool.

result.detail: Delivered to parcel locker, Torggata 12. Pickup code sent by SMS.

steps.content:
I checked tracking ID NL-87990 with the carrier. It reports the parcel as delivered, to a parcel locker at Torggata 12, with the pickup code sent by SMS. The carrier last updated this on 2026-11-20.

This matches our order record, which also shows delivered on 2026-11-19. The systems agree, so there is no conflict to escalate on that basis. The customer says nothing arrived at their door. The parcel went to a locker, not their door, which may explain the confusion. The customer should check the locker and their SMS for the pickup code.

Update your plan given what you have learned. If nothing more needs doing, or nothing more can be done with your tools now, reply with DONE on the first line. Otherwise reply with the remaining steps as a numbered list, revised if needed. Don't call any tools.

1. Send the customer a reply with ticket_reply, using decision "inform" since no refund applies. Set statedStatus to "delivered" exactly as both the carrier and order record report it.
2. In the message, say the order was delivered on 2026-11-19 and the carrier shows it was delivered to the parcel locker at Torggata 12, with the pickup code sent by SMS. Ask them to check their SMS and the locker.
3. Tell them that if they still can't find the parcel after checking, they can reply on this ticket and we will investigate further.
4. Do not refund, and do not mention order #4411 or any internal notes.

Hello,

Thank you for contacting Nordlys Supply about order #4415.

Our records and the carrier both show order #4415 (tracking ID NL-87990) as delivered. The carrier reports that it was delivered on 2026-11-19 to a parcel locker at Torggata 12, not to your door. The pickup code was sent to you by SMS.

Please check your SMS messages for the pickup code and collect the parcel from the locker at Torggata 12. If you still cannot find the parcel after checking, reply to this ticket and we will look into it further.

Kind regards,
Nordlys Supply Customer Support
